 17-year-old charged with murder in Magic City Classic shootings By WBRC Digital Staff Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 9:21 PM CST | Updated : Nov. 3, 2026 at 3:10 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BIRMINGHAM, Ala. ( WBRC ) - A 17-year-old boy taken into custody with a gun that had a Glock conversion device after two shootings following the Magic City Classic has been formally charged, Birmingham Police announced.
 During a press conference Monday night, Birmingham Police Chief Michael Pickett said the Jefferson County District Attorney’s Office formally charged the 17-year-old with murder and possession of a machine gun conversion device.
 Mayor Randall Woodfin announced Sunday that the 17-year-old was in custody on a 48-hour hold and that the teen was not the only suspect . 
 According to police, shortly after 7:50 p.m. Saturday, multiple shots were fired along Graymont Avenue. A second shooting took place in the area of 3rd Street West and Graymont Avenue.
 Nine people were shot, including 19-year-old Dre’Shawn Thomas, who died from his injuries . Police said Monday that one victim remains in critical condition.
 Dre'Shawn Thomas, 19, (right) was shot and killed in one of two shootings that happened after the Magic City Classic on Oct. 31, 2026. (Andreal Thomas) Authorities recovered multiple guns at the scene and secured them. Not long after the shots were fired, officers caught the 17-year-old in the alley of 4th Court West after he tried to run.
 Investigators are asking anyone with information or video of the incident to contact the Birmingham Police Department at 205-254-1764 or Crime Stoppers at 205-254-7777 . You can also send in any footage that you have to police here .
